solubility.notes: Slow sustained dissolution over weeks. Prilled form dissolves faster than powdered. Moist soil accelerates dissolution — Oak Vista April 1 application benefited from Easter rain.

bioavailability.mechanism: Ca2+ and SO4 2- enter soil solution as gypsum dissolves. Ca2+ moves to roots via mass flow in transpiration stream. Competes with coco coir exchange sites — elevated concentration drives mass action displacement of K+ and Na+.

solubility.notes: Highly hygroscopic — absorbs moisture from air. Rapid ionic dissociation in solution. RTU formulation at 1.6% is pre-diluted to safe foliar concentration.

bioavailability.mechanism: Rapid ionic Ca2+ uptake through open stomata. High solubility enables fast apoplastic distribution to cell walls. Speed advantage over chelated forms — immediate delivery to developing fruit.

properties.berPreventionRole: Week 1 and 3 of alternating protocol — fast ionic Ca delivery

solubility.notes: Fine 200-mesh powder dissolves rapidly on first irrigation. 2 cups = 2 lbs for this product — critical density note. ChatGPT volume error caused Box 1 over-application April 2026.

bioavailability.mechanism: K+ and SO4 2- immediately available in soil solution. K+ absorbed via root transporters. Competes with Ca2+ and Mg2+ for uptake at elevated concentrations — excess K reduces effective Ca and Mg availability.

solubility.notes: Elemental sulfur itself is insoluble. Must be oxidized to sulfate by Thiobacillus bacteria before becoming plant-available. Rate accelerates above 77°F soil temperature.

bioavailability.mechanism: Thiobacillus oxidizes S to H2SO4. In limestone-containing soils: H2SO4 + CaCO3 → CaSO4 + H2O + CO2 — produces in-situ gypsum. Net effect: slow sulfate delivery with pH buffering by limestone.

properties.phEffect: Mild acidification — largely neutralized by limestone in Oak Vista soil

solubility.notes: Highly soluble — rapid ionic dissociation. Applied as Day 2 of monthly drench protocol. Separated from Day 1 CalMag OAC chelate to prevent sulfate interference with chelate absorption.

bioavailability.mechanism: Mg2+ absorbed by roots and foliage. Foliar uptake effective for rapid chlorophyll replenishment. Separated from chelate application — sulfate ions compete with organic acid chelate receptor sites.

properties.berProtocolRole: Day 2 of monthly drench — sulfate + magnesium
properties.separationRationale: Applied Day 2 after CalMag OAC Day 1 — sulfate does not interfere with next-day chelate application

solubility.notes: Very sparingly soluble. Dissolves slowly releasing Ca2+ and buffering pH. Elevated in Oak Vista soil — 1.7% Box 1, 2.9% backyard (post-hole subsoil). Optimum below 0.50%.

bioavailability.mechanism: Very slow Ca2+ release as CaCO3 dissolves. pH buffering reaction with acids: CaCO3 + H2SO4 → CaSO4 + H2O + CO2. Neutralizes sulfuric acid from sulfur oxidation — produces in-situ gypsum.

properties.oakVistaSource: Native Chico Valley parent material + post-hole subsoil
properties.phBufferingRole: Neutralizes acid from sulfur oxidation — limits pH reduction
properties.contraindicatedAmendment: Do not add lime — pH already optimal at 7.2

solubility.notes: Structural component — not dissolved. Calcium cross-links pectin chains in primary cell walls. Permanent structural deposit — cannot be redistributed once formed.

bioavailability.mechanism: Calcium incorporated into pectin chains during active cell division. Requires continuous Ca2+ supply at moment of cell wall formation. Calcium is immobile in tissue — each new cell requires fresh delivery. Interruption produces BER.

properties.berRelevance: BER occurs when Ca2+ supply insufficient for calcium pectate formation during rapid fruit cell division
properties.mobilityInPlant: IMMOBILE — cannot be redistributed from older tissue to new growth
properties.criticalWindow: Blossom set through first 3 weeks of fruit development
properties.chicoRisk: High — summer heat accelerates cell division beyond Ca2+ supply rate

solubility.notes: Fully miscible. 18-month shelf life. NPK 0-0-0 — zero phosphorus critical given Oak Vista phosphorus excess.

bioavailability.mechanism: Organic acid ligands protect Ca2+ and Mg2+ from precipitation and competing ions. Chelate penetrates waxy cuticle — available even when stomata closed in heat. Organic acids chaperone Ca2+ directly to cell wall synthesis sites.

properties.berProtocolRole: Week 2 and 4 of alternating protocol — chelated cuticular Ca+Mg
properties.advantageOverIonic: Penetrates cuticle when stomata closed — heat resilient

solubility.notes: Fully miscible with water. Naturally produced by ants and some plants. Varroa miticide via fumigation — vapor phase kills mites in capped brood cells.

bioavailability.mechanism: Vapor phase penetrates capped brood cells — kills Varroa mites on contact with vapor. Efficacy driven by vapor pressure which increases nonlinearly with temperature.

volatilization.efficacyNotes: Below 50°F insufficient vapor for mite kill. 50-85°F effective range. Vapor pressure increases rapidly above 70°F.
volatilization.safetyNotes: Above 85°F dangerous vapor concentration in hive. Chico summer peak 105°F makes formic acid HIGH RISK June-September. Consider Apiguard (thymol) for August treatment.

safety.applicationConstraints: Do not apply when ambient temperature exceeds 85°F. Corrosive — gloves and eye protection required. Verify California CDPR approval status with Dadant Chico before purchase.

properties.chicoRisk: HIGH — summer temperatures exceed safe application window June-September
properties.californiaStatus: Verify CDPR approval with Dadant Chico before procurement
properties.alternativeForChico: Apiguard (thymol) preferred for August-September treatment window

solubility.notes: Moderately soluble. Applied as dribble treatment (aqueous solution) or vaporization. Dribble most effective during broodless period.

bioavailability.mechanism: Contact kill of phoretic Varroa mites on adult bees. Dribble method: saturated bees groom each other spreading treatment. Vapor method: oxalic acid vapor condenses on mites. Most effective when no capped brood present.

volatilization.efficacyNotes: Low vapor pressure — sublimation requires heating equipment. Effective across wide temperature range unlike formic acid.
volatilization.safetyNotes: Irritant — respiratory protection required for vaporization method. Safer temperature profile than formic acid for Chico summers.

safety.applicationConstraints: Respiratory protection required for vaporization. Most effective during broodless period (winter or after artificial swarm). Verify California CDPR approval with Dadant Chico.

properties.californiaStatus: Verify CDPR approval with Dadant Chico
properties.advantageOverFormic: Wider temperature safety window — viable in Chico conditions

solubility.notes: Naturally occurring phenol from thyme. Sparingly soluble in water but volatile. Apiguard formulation is 25% thymol in gel carrier for controlled slow release.

bioavailability.mechanism: Thymol vapor fills hive cavity and contacts Varroa mites. Efficacy directly proportional to volatilization rate which depends on temperature. Gel carrier moderates release rate.

volatilization.efficacyNotes: Below 59°F insufficient volatilization — treatment fails. Most effective 65-95°F. Chico late August/early September is optimal application window.
volatilization.safetyNotes: Natural compound — safer than formic acid. Bees tolerate well within temperature range. Some colony agitation possible at high concentrations.

safety.applicationConstraints: Temperature must be above 59°F for efficacy. Do not apply during honey flow — thymol taints honey. Remove honey super before treatment.

properties.chicoApplicationWindow: Late August through September — temperatures moderating from summer peak
properties.advantageOverFormic: Safer temperature profile for Chico climate — viable when formic acid is too risky
properties.honeyWarning: Remove honey super before treatment — thymol taints honey

solubility.notes: Requires soap emulsifier for aqueous application. Breaks down rapidly in UV light — evening application maximizes residual activity. 5-7 day residual in soil.

bioavailability.mechanism: Disrupts insect molting hormone (ecdysone) — insects cannot complete molt and die. Also feeding deterrent. Slower mode of action than contact insecticides — population decline over days not hours.

safety.applicationConstraints: Apply after 7 PM when bee foragers have returned to hive. Harmful to bees when wet. Safe when dry. OMRI listed. Repeat every 5-7 days x3 applications for thrips control.

properties.applicationRate: 2 tbsp neem oil per gallon with 2 tbsp dish soap emulsifier
properties.targetPests: Thrips, spider mites, aphids, whitefly, fungus gnats
properties.oakVistaUse: Straw mulch drench for thrips control — April 7 2026 TSWV outbreak
properties.uvDegradation: Breaks down within 24-48 hours in sunlight — evening application required

solubility.notes: Fully miscible. Contact kill only — no residual. Also used as emulsifier for neem oil applications. Equivalent mechanism to commercial insecticidal soap.

bioavailability.mechanism: Disrupts cell membrane integrity of soft-bodied insects on direct contact. Penetrates insect cuticle causing desiccation and cell lysis. Effective on thrips, mites, aphids. No systemic activity.

safety.applicationConstraints: Apply after 7 PM — harmful to bees on direct contact when wet. Safe when dry.

properties.emulsifierRole: Emulsifies neem oil in water for combined treatment
properties.oakVistaProduct: Kirkland Ultra Shine dish soap (equivalent mechanism to commercial insecticidal soap)
properties.traditionalUse: Traditional pest control remedy — scientifically validated contact insecticide
